programme.title: Why'd They Wear That?
programme.desc: Clinton Kelly and Stacy London celebrate scene-stealing fashion moments from classic and cult films in this special episode. Rather than critiquing real people's style, the hosts examine fictional characters whose looks left lasting impressions. Stacy's selections include Cher's transformative opera look in Moonstruck, Michelle Pfeiffer's Pink Lady perfection in Grease 2, and Annette Bening in a show-stopping red dress from The Grifters. Clinton chooses Shelley Duvall's impeccably accessorized outfit in The Shining, Grace Kelly's elegant black-and-white ensemble in Rear Window, and the neon-outlined muses in Xanadu. The hosts provide detailed analysis of costume design, silhouettes, proportions, and the emotional resonance these looks achieved on screen.

They examine each look in detail, from the strapless hot pink lamé dress at the Candy Bar club to the oversized tuxedo blazer in her final scene, discussing how the wardrobe reflects both 1980s fashion trends and Lisa's character arc from object of fantasy to respected individual.

programme.title: Why'd They Wear That?

The hosts dissect multiple scenes featuring Jane Fonda's uptight office worker, Lily Tomlin's chic and coordinated Violet Newstead, and Dolly Parton's glamorous Doralee Rhodes. They discuss the film's influence on their own fashion sensibilities during their formative years, analyzing everything from the iconic opening-day suit to the final red, white, and blue power looks. The discussion covers tailoring techniques, the challenges of dressing different body types, 1980s fashion trends like the Adidas tracksuit, and how costume choices reinforce each character's personality and arc.

programme.title: Why'd They Wear That?
programme.desc: Clinton Kelly and Stacy London break down the costume design of Sydney Pollack's 1982 comedy Tootsie, designed by Ruth Morley. The hosts discuss how the film's wardrobe serves the plot of struggling actor Michael Dorsey reinventing himself as the soap opera star Dorothy Michaels, analyzing specific outfits worn by the main cast including Dustin Hoffman, Jessica Lange, and Teri Garr. Key segments include examining Garr's chic party look, the strategic use of high necklines and flowing skirts to conceal Hoffman's masculine features, a standout costume montage featuring magazine covers and an iconic red sequined dress, and Jessica Lange's effortlessly chic final scene outfit. The hosts debate costume choices, offer styling advice, and ultimately praise the montage as essential to the film's fashion appeal.
